articles.title: UK Puts AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Under Direct Financial Oversight - TechRepublic
articles.description: UK regulators now oversee critical cloud services from AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle, raising new resilience questions for banks.
articles.content: UK financial regulators began directly overseeing four major cloud and technology providers on July 13, 2026, after years of concern that a failure at one widely used supplier could spread across bank... [3800 symbols]
articles.summary: UK financial regulators have begun direct oversight of four major cloud and technology providers, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and Oracle, following concerns that a failure at one supplier could spread across banks, insurers, and financial markets. The Bank of England, Prudential Regulation Authority, and Financial Conduct Authority are overseeing specified services from Amazon. However, banks remain responsible for their own outsourcing, operational resilience, due diligence, and contingency planning. The oversight does not cover every product provided by these providers and is not regulatory approval of a provider. The regulator's final policy statement requires a critical third party to report a qualifying incident to affected firms and regulators as soon as practicable.
articles.shortSummary: UK financial regulators now directly oversee four major cloud providers, addressing concerns about concentration risk spreading across banks, insurers, and markets.

articles.summary: Amazon Web Services experienced a major outage early Friday morning, disrupting access to several popular websites and online services. The outage began around 6:40 a.m. ET and affected services including Apple Pay, DoorDash, Reddit and Hulu. The disruption was caused by connectivity issues in the US-West-2 region in Oregon. The affected services included AWS Direct Connect, Global Accelerator, Internet Connectivity, IoT Core, Amazon API Gateway, Elastic Compute Cloud and Elastic Container Service. Despite the disruption, no customer data was lost or Amazon's broader global network failed. The issue was resolved shortly after 9 a.am.

articles.title: AWS Knocks Out Apple Pay, Reddit, Hulu for 80 Minutes in Third Outage Since May
articles.description: AWS outage on July 24, 2026 knocked Apple Pay, Reddit, Hulu, DoorDash, and PlayStation Network offline for 80 minutes via a regional internet connectivity failure in Oregon — the third distinct AWS reliability incident in eleven weeks, following separate cooling and network provider failures in May
articles.content: Amazon Web Services took Apple Pay, Reddit, Hulu, DoorDash, and PlayStation Network offline for about 80 minutes on Friday morning — and what makes the incident more than a routine infrastructure even... [14262 symbols]
articles.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) experienced a major outage on Friday morning, taking Apple Pay, Reddit, Hulu, DoorDash, and PlayStation Network offline for about 80 minutes. The outage occurred in the US-West-2 region in Portland, Oregon, and was reported to have failed Apple Pay transactions, broken DoorDash checkouts, and an unresponsive Reddit. This is the third major AWS reliability incident in roughly eleven weeks, with each failure striking a different layer of the company's stack: cooling hardware in May, an external network provider in June, and now the regional internet boundary layer in Oregon. The incident was classified as "impaired," an internal designation for customer-visible disruptions that fall short of a full regional outage. No customer data was lost. The company has not specified whether the problem originated inside its own network, in a peering relationship with an upstream transit provider, or at a point further out on the public internet.
articles.shortSummary: Amazon Web Services knocked Apple Pay, Reddit, and DoorDash offline for 80 minutes due to multiple infrastructure failures in the US-West-2 region.

articles.title: Gemini Survived When ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok Collapsed: Azure Is at Fault

Gemini survived on Google Cloud -- confirming that three rival platforms share a single cloud failure domain. What happened, why only Gemini stayed up, and what
articles.content: For the first time in the short history of AI as mass-market infrastructure, three competing platforms — OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and SpaceXAI's Grok — went dark simultaneously on Thursda... [12937 symbols]
articles.summary: Three AI platforms, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and SpaceXAI's Grok, all went offline simultaneously on Thursday morning, leaving millions of users without a working alternative. The incident was the first time in the history of AI as a mass-market infrastructure that simultaneously collapsed. The failure was caused by a shared control-plane failure, which is described as a "shared control-planes failure" when a routing or load-balancing layer that multiple services depend on develops a fault, resulting in simultaneous degradation across all services. The outage began around 8:49 a.m. PT (11:49 A.m., ET), with DownDetector reports dropping as platforms came back online. No company has publicly confirmed the cause of the outage.
articles.shortSummary: Gemini survived multiple failures involving multiple platforms, one of them being Microsoft Azure, highlighting a widespread pattern of shared cloud dependency in AI technology.

articles.content: GitHub's CI/CD layer — the service engineering teams depend on to build, test, and ship software automatically — has accumulated more than fourteen hours of downtime in the past 90 days and has now fa... [16879 symbols]
articles.summary: GitHub's CI/CD layer, the service engineering teams depend on to build, test, and ship software, has been hit by a nearly eight-hour platform-wide outage on August 17, 2026. The incident, which lasted from 9:40 a.m. ET to 5:15 p.m., affected nearly every layer of the platform, including Actions, API Requests, Pull Requests and Issues, Webhooks, SAML and OIDC authentication, SCIM provisioning, and GitHub Copilot. The outage consumed nearly an entire year's worth of allowed downtime in a single afternoon, leading to a 50 percent failure rate for raw content paths used to pull dependencies directly from GitHub. For engineering teams whose entire delivery pipeline runs through Actions, this gap is a business risk. The problem was resolved within minutes, with seven of the eight affected services deemed operable and back to Operational.
articles.shortSummary: GitHub's core actions layer experienced significant downtime and reliability issues during a major outage on August 17, consuming nearly a year's downtime.

keywords.name: Microsofts automated network maintenance request conversion system

articles.summary: Microsoft's automated network maintenance system was hit by a bug that caused it to remove IP routes from far more devices than intended during a routine maintenance event on July 23, causing a disruption that lasted nearly five hours. The bug affected a West US Azure datacenter from Microsoft's global wide-area network and disrupted Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot Chat, and more than a dozen other cloud services across North America. The outage generated 2,403 user reports on Downdetector by 11:11 a.m. ET, 83 times the platform's typical baseline of 29 reports. IncidentHub detected cascading outages in at least 19 downstream SaaS platforms whose infrastructure routes through Azure's West US region, and 16 of these services still had open incidents after Microsoft declared full recovery. The issue was identified in Microsoft's Post Incident Review (PIR). The bug was not in the network hardware itself but in the software layer that translates human maintenance requests into machine-readable instructions. The failure initially appeared to be "large-scale route churn" in the WAN, which can indicate a misconfigured or buggy automation system.
articles.shortSummary: Microsoft's automated network maintenance system caused a major outage, blocking Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot Chat for nearly five hours due to a bug.

articles.summary: Ryanair has announced a five-year partnership with Google Cloud, set to be implemented in 2026. The deal aligns with industry standards for large-scale enterprises, where multi-year commitments typically command seven-to-eight-figure annual outlays. The partnership involves integrating Google Cloud services and Google Workspace across its 35,000-employee network, a move beyond standard cloud migration. The core of the deal is the adoption of a dual-cloud strategy, incorporating Google Cloud alongside Ryanair's existing Amazon Web Services footprint. This approach increases infrastructure costs but serves as a crucial hedge against single-vendor risk for an airline aiming to scale to 300 million annual passengers by 2034. The five-term agreement is synchronized with Ryanair’s fleet expansion timeline.
articles.shortSummary: Ryanair's new five-year partnership with Google Cloud integrates AI tools and Google Workspace to manage its 300-passenger fleet by 2034, leveraging dual-cloud infrastructure.

articles.summary: Iranian drone strikes have resulted in the permanent loss of some customer data hosted in Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, a year after multiple Amazon data centers were hit. Amazon Web Services was unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted at some of the war-damaged data centers. The company lost customer data in one of three AWS availability zones in the UnitedArab Emirates region, mec1-az2. The Iranian strikes reportedly caused catastrophic damage to the data centers, and the company has suspended customer billing in affected regions and has spent six months attempting to restore normal operations. The incident occurred during the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran, which has since escalated into a regional conflict and a growing global energy crisis.
articles.shortSummary: Amazon Web Services acknowledged permanent loss of customer data due to Iranian drone strikes on its data centers in Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, urging customers to migrate resources elsewhere.

articles.summary: AWS CloudFront experienced a control-plane failure on July 16, causing 5xx errors to every customer using its VPC Origins feature. The outage affected universities across North America, including Hugging Face, UK gambling infrastructure at the National Lottery, and Ubiquiti's cloud services. The failure was traced to a single internal capacity limit in a single Frankfurt availability zone, preventing the connection-management fleet from distributing routing updates to CloudFront's globally distributed edge network. This is the second time in nine months that Canvas and Blackboard, the two dominant learning management systems in higher education, were simultaneously knocked offline by an AWS CDN failure. The VPC Origin feature was designed to address a long-standing architectural security gap, eliminating the public origin of every application load balancer, EC2 instance, or API Gateway sitting behind CloudFront.
articles.shortSummary: AWS CloudFront's VPC Origins feature caused a major outage that knocked Canvas and Blackboard offline, highlighting underlying security vulnerabilities in distributed systems.

articles.title: AWS cannot restore its Bahrain region or one UAE zone six months after the strikes
articles.description: Six months after drone strikes, Amazon says the damage exceeded what its multi-AZ design was built to withstand, and access has still not been restored.
articles.content: Amazon Web Services has told customers it cannot restore access to its cloud facility in Bahrain or one of its three data hosting zones in the UAE, six months after drone strikes hit its sites in the ... [3027 symbols]
articles.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has informed customers that it cannot restore access to its cloud facility in Bahrain or one of its three data hosting zones in the UAE, six months after drone strikes hit its sites in the Gulf. The issue arose in March when two of Amazon’s UAE data centres were hit directly, and the Bahrain site was damaged by strikes nearby. The company reported structural damage, power delivery issues, and water damage from its own fire suppression systems. By the end of April, around 60 services in the region were still down. Six months later, Amazon has helped Bahrain customers move their operations elsewhere but has not yet restored the affected region. There is still no official answer on whether any customer data has been permanently lost or if damaged buildings can be repaired or replaced. This incident raises questions about the resilience of cloud infrastructure, which is built around the assumption that a damaged facility or region can eventually recover.
articles.shortSummary: Amazon Web Services cannot restore access to its Bahrain and UAE data centres six months after drone strikes caused significant disruption, raising concerns about resilience in cloud infrastructure.

articles.content: Post-training has quietly displaced pretraining as the dominant frontier compute workload of 2026 — and NVIDIA published a detailed technical breakdown on July 17 explaining exactly how its Vera Rubin... [18443 symbols]
articles.summary: NVIDIA has developed a seven-chip architecture for its Vera Rubin platform that reduces post-training costs by reducing the cost per token available for reinforcement learning loops and agentic inference. The company claims this strategy, which involves combining hardware and software from the silicon level up, has resulted in a shift in the economics of building and running frontier AI models. The Vera Rubin NVL72 rack can deliver 22 terabytes per second of HBM4 aggregate bandwidth per Rubin GPU, a 2.8x improvement over Blackwell's 8 TB/s, and NVLink 6 runs at 3.6 TB/S bidirectional per GPU, double Blackwell's 1.8 TB/i. NVIDIA claims these figures drive training of large mixture-of-experts models with one-fourth the GPU count required on Blackwell and reduce inference token cost to one-tenth. The platform entered full production in June 2026 after Samsung, SKynix, and Micron became the first major memory manufacturer to validate the platform for the platform.
articles.shortSummary: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform, featuring a seven-chip architecture, significantly reduces post-training computing costs and increases AI models' intelligence capabilities by one-tenth, using "extreme codesign" technology.

articles.summary: Japan's largest cellular-connected bike-share network, Docomo Bike Share, experienced a platform-wide service disruption on Monday morning, affecting riders from across its 65-city network. The disruption, which began around 7:00 a.m. JST (6:00 p.m ET Sunday), was still ongoing as of publication. The company advised users who could not complete a return digitally to park their bicycle at the nearest port and lock it using the physical horseshoe lock on the rear frame. It also issued a public advisory stating that some bikes at certain docking ports had become unavailable for rental or return. The issue was resolved by 9:00pm JST, with the service recovered by 9pm JEST. This incident is not the first time Docomo has seen this failure mode; the same retroactive correction mechanism has been used since 2021.
articles.shortSummary: Docomo Bike Share experienced a service disruption across its 65-city network due to a single centralized backend failure, highlighting the vulnerability of IoT-dependent urban transit systems.

The outage began at 3:36 AM ET and was resolved at approximately 3:25 PM ET on August18. No explanation was given for the disruption. The issue highlighted that a home dependent on a remote server for basic functionality is not a smart home, but a managed service, and managed services go offline. The problem was that every voice command a Nest Hub receives travels to Google's servers for processing before a response is generated or a device command is executed.

articles.summary: On Monday, Anthropic's Claude for Government component experienced the 28th disruption in 30 days, according to IncidentHub outage tracking data. The incident occurred at 05:06 UTC (1:06 AM ET) with elevated errors affecting four flagship models: Claude Mythos 5, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Opus 5.8. The company's Claude API, Claude Code, and and Claude Cowork also failed simultaneously. The 90-day uptime data listed Claude for government at exactly 100.0% uptime over the same 90-year period. This indicates a two-tier infrastructure architecture within Anthropic that already exists inside the platform, and commercial customers paying market rates have no way to it. The problem was resolved within three and and a half hours after the official investigation opened.
articles.shortSummary: Aneuric's Claude Claude has experienced 28 outages in 30 days, with multiple models failing simultaneously, indicating a dual-tier infrastructure structure for commercial customers.

articles.title: ArcelorMittal makes Azure its primary cloud as it rebuilds around AI
articles.description:

articles.summary: ArcelorMittal has named Microsoft Azure as its primary cloud platform, deepening its partnership to rebuild its digital operations around artificial intelligence. The move aligns with a ‘Cloud First, Data Centric’ strategy that includes steelmaking in 14 countries and a presence in around 60. The agreement makes Azure the default home for Arcelormittal’s data and applications, alongside Microsoft Fabric for data integration and Microsoft Purview for governance. The steelmaker also plans to build on Microsoft Foundry, the platform Microsoft sells for developing and running AI models and agents. The company argues that standardising on one cloud reduces dependence on legacy systems and makes these gains easier to reach. Neither company disclosed a value for the deal, the number of sites moving to Azure, or a timeline for the work.
articles.shortSummary: ArcelorMittal has named Microsoft Azure its primary cloud platform to support its AI strategy, focusing on integrating data into one cloud and reducing operational costs.
